headline_as_shown: MCU trimming 28.7 -> 7.4 ms per chip (3.9x faster)
rows_evaluated: 1,684 dies on 4 held-out wafers (MA1-W01, MA2-W05, MA3-W02, MA3-W04)
split_and_seed: GroupShuffleSplit by wafer_id, 25% of the base version's wafers held out, random_state=42 (src/common.py wafer_split)
model_or_method: Random Forest x3 (bg, hsi, ldo), models/trim_models.joblib
metric_definition: ms per chip = sum over the 3 trims of tries x assumed ms per measurement. Today: dataset *_conv_iterations. AI: 1 try if the predicted code is exact, 2 if 1 code off, else 1 + DAC bits (falls back to the full search)
assumptions: ms per measurement assumed: bandgap 1.2, HSI 2.0, LDO 1.0. No tester, index or handler overhead
why_different: the dataset author's simpler baseline; reported per trim as iterations, not ms per chip

headline_as_shown: 85% of SoC chips skip the speed test, 0 over-graded
rows_evaluated: 1,540 dies on 5 held-out wafers; margin chosen on 1,232 validation dies
split_and_seed: GroupShuffleSplit by wafer_id, 25% of the base version's wafers held out, random_state=42 (src/common.py wafer_split); 80 MHz margin chosen on validation wafers (0 escapes), then applied once to the held-out wafers
model_or_method: Ridge speed models (models/soc_models.joblib) + 80 MHz margin; chips within 80 MHz of a product boundary get the real speed test
metric_definition: skip share = chips more than 80 MHz from every product boundary. Over-graded = sold as a faster product than the full speed test allows
assumptions: speed test 450 ms per chip (dataset mean)
range_across_wafers: 0 of 1,540 over-graded; with 0 events the 95% upper bound is about 0.19%

headline_as_shown: SoC worst-core Vmin predicted within 4.2 mV typical error (median baseline 27 mV); 25 mV margin, 0 of 1,540 under-predicted
rows_evaluated: 1,540 dies on 5 held-out wafers; margin chosen on 1,232 validation dies
split_and_seed: GroupShuffleSplit by wafer_id, 25% of wafers held out, random_state=42; validation wafers split the same way inside the training wafers
model_or_method: Ridge regression on ring oscillator, critical-path delay, IDDQ, 5 process monitors and die position (models/vmin_models.joblib, notebook 07)
metric_definition: mean absolute error between measured and predicted worst-core Vmin at 2 GHz (highest Vmin among working cores). Margin = smallest whole mV with zero under-predicted chips on validation wafers
assumptions: in this dataset the AVS voltage bin is set from speed, so the Vmin model does not change the bin logic
range_across_wafers: 3.8 to 4.5 mV (median 4.2), each of 20 wafers held out in turn; 0 under-predicted at 25 mV on every wafer

headline_as_shown: SoC chips that skip the speed test: 0 of 1,306 given a lower AVS voltage bin than they need; 34% exact bin, 66% higher (mean +12.7 mV)
rows_evaluated: 1,306 of the 1,308 dies that skip the speed test (the 2 others get a different product, counted in SOC_SKIP), 5 held-out wafers
split_and_seed: GroupShuffleSplit by wafer_id, 25% of wafers held out, random_state=42
model_or_method: AVS bin from the product spec's voltage rule applied to the predicted speed minus the 80 MHz margin (src/soc.py margin_split, avs_offset)
metric_definition: bin from the prediction minus the bin the measured speed needs; one bin = 12.5 mV
assumptions: AVS bin is derived from speed in this dataset; the margin was chosen for products, not separately for bins

headline_as_shown: MCU temperature sensor 110 C point predicted for MCU-A/B: 3.0 -> 0.82 C typical error, 95% within +-2 C
rows_evaluated: trained on 842 MCU-C dies (2 wafers, the only version measured hot); scored on 7,578 MCU-A/B dies (18 wafers)
split_and_seed: train on MCU-C, predict MCU-A and MCU-B (product-version transfer, no wafer on both sides)
model_or_method: Ridge regression on the 30 C reading, 5 process monitors and die position (models/tsense_models.joblib, notebook 08)
metric_definition: mean absolute temperature error the chip would report at a true 110 C, two-point calibration with the predicted hot point. Baseline: one fixed rise (MCU-C mean)
assumptions: 89% of MCU-A/B dies lie outside MCU-C's oxide-thickness range, so the model extrapolates; the true hot points are used only for scoring
range_across_wafers: 0.78 to 0.87 C over 18 wafers; within MCU-C (2 wafers) Ridge only matches the fixed rise
